1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
21	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
22	
23	## State (measured 2026-07-27)
24	
25	- **172 modules, 124,300 lines.**  **26 `sorry`** remain, spread over 11 modules;
26	  the rest are locally sorry-free.
27	- A warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` is **green**: 8,723 jobs, exit 0.
28	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
29	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
30	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
31	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
32	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
33	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
34	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
35	  synthesise the instance.  Run

77	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard

2	\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean
4	
5	\section{Setup and motivation}
6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7	
8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17	
18	\medskip
19	
20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23	
24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32	of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33	
34	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35	separably closed field, from the open loci
36	\[
37	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38	\]
39	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme.
44	
45	The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
46	quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
47	the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
48	(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
49	only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
50	that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
51	Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
52	mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
53	consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
54	
55	\medskip
56	
57	\textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
58	the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
59	works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
60	\(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
61	representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
62	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
63	Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
64	and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
65	(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
66	base change), then the comparison maps
67	\[
68	  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
69	  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
70	\]
71	are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
72	plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
73	allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
74	
75	The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
76	even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
77	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
78	formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
79	
80	\begin{enumerate}
81	  \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
82	    hypothesis. This is the formulation of
83	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
84	    in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
85	    proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
86	    rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
87	    over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
88	    hypothesis.
89	  \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
90	    rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
91	    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
92	    would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
93	    the \'etale site.
94	\end{enumerate}
95	
96	Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
97	being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
98	side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
99	
100	Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
101	rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
102	\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
103

244	  over \(k\) \emph{with a \(k\)-rational point}
245	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}). Then the relative Picard functor
246	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp} --- which under the
247	  rational-point hypothesis coincides with its \'etale sheafification
248	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), by Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 --- is representable by a
249	  \(k\)-scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over

258	  We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
259	  \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
260	  comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of
261	  \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme} and the relative Picard functor of
262	  \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
263	  correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.
264	
265	  \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
266	  By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
267	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}
268	  \mathcal O_{C \times_k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology
269	  and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of
270	  \(C\times_k T/T\)), the comparison map
271	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) \to \Pic_{(C/k)\et}(T)\) is bijective for all
272	  \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the \'etale sheaf
273	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which is what Kleiman's theorem produces; the same
274	  scheme then represents \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
275	
276	  \emph{Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.}
277	  For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq
278	  \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) be the \'etale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are
279	  represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) with
280	  \(\chi(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the
281	  Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation
282	  \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi\) form a
283	  disjoint open cover of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (openness via Kleiman's
284	  flat-base-change argument, \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change} / Stacks Tag 02KH;
285	  cf.\ EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to
286	  represent each \(P^\phi\) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective
287	  \(k\)-schemes.
288	
289	  \emph{Step 2: bound twists by \(m\)-regularity.}
290	  Given \(\phi\), fix \(m\) large enough that the \(T\)-points of \(P^\phi\) are
291	  representable by \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) satisfying
292	  \(R^i \pi_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0\) for all \(i \ge 1\), \(n \ge m\). Twisting
293	  by \(\mathcal{O}_C(m)\) defines an automorphism of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
294	  that carries \(P^\phi\) to \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) for \(\phi_0(n) := \phi(m + n)\).
295	  Hence it suffices to represent each \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) by a quasi-projective
296	  \(k\)-scheme.

298	  \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}
299	  Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
300	  of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
301	  is representable by an open subscheme of \(\Hilb_{C/k}\) (and hence by an
302	  open subscheme of the Quot scheme of \cref{thm:quot_representable}), and
303	  is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along
304	  \(P^{\phi_0}_0 \hookrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) yields an open
305	  subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi_0}_0 \times_{\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
306	  of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection
307	  \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi_0}_0\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves:
308	  given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda\) of \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) represented by an \'etale
309	  cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times_k
310	  T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle
311	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to
312	  \(\mathcal{Q} := \pi_{T'*}\mathcal{L}'\) is smooth over \(T'\); an \'etale
313	  cover \(T_1 \to T'\) admits a \(T'\)-map \(T_1 \to \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q})\)
314	  (EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii)) whose composition with the universal divisor map
315	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to Z\) produces the required \(T_1\)-point of \(Z\).
316	  Moreover, the first projection \(Z \times_{P^{\phi_0}_0} Z \to Z\) is
317	  smooth and proper.
318	
319	  \emph{Step 4: descend by the smooth-proper quotient lemma.}
320	  Apply Kleiman~\S 4, Lem.~4.9: given a surjection \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
321	  of \'etale sheaves with \(Z\) quasi-projective, \(R := Z \times_P Z\)
322	  representable, and the first projection \(R \to Z\) smooth and proper,
323	  \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective scheme. In our case
324	  \(P = P^{\phi_0}_0\), \(Z\) and \(R\) as above, so \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) is
325	  quasi-projective. Reassembling over \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\) and
326	  over \(m\), the disjoint union of representable \(P^\phi\) pieces represents
327	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\). The total scheme is separated (as a disjoint
328	  union of separated quasi-projectives) and locally of finite type. This
329	  is Kleiman~\S 4, Cor.~4.18.3 in the \(S = \Spec k\),
330	  \(X = C\) complete case.
331	\end{proof}

abelian variety of dimension \(g\). This is the load-bearing A.3.vii

1	\chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
2	\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean
4	
5	\section{Setup and motivation}
6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7	
8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17	
18	\medskip
19	
20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23	
24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32	of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33	
34	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35	separably closed field, from the open loci
36	\[
37	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38	\]
39	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme.
44	
45	The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
46	quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
47	the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
48	(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
49	only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
50	that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
51	Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
52	mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
53	consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
54	
55	\medskip
56	
57	\textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
58	the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
59	works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
60	\(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
61	representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
62	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
63	Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
64	and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
65	(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
66	base change), then the comparison maps
67	\[
68	  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
69	  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
70	\]
71	are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
72	plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
73	allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
74	
75	The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
76	even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
77	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
78	formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
79	
80	\begin{enumerate}
81	  \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
82	    hypothesis. This is the formulation of
83	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
84	    in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
85	    proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
86	    rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
87	    over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
88	    hypothesis.
89	  \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
90	    rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
91	    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
92	    would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
93	    the \'etale site.
94	\end{enumerate}
95	
96	Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
97	being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
98	side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
99	
100	Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
101	rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
102	\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
103

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.

1	\chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
2	\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean
4	
5	\section{Setup and motivation}
6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7	
8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17	
18	\medskip
19	
20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23	
24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32	of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33	
34	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35	separably closed field, from the open loci
36	\[
37	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38	\]
39	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme.
44	
45	The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
46	quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
47	the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
48	(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
49	only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
50	that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
51	Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
52	mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
53	consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
54	
55	\medskip
56	
57	\textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
58	the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
59	works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
60	\(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
61	representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
62	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
63	Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
64	and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
65	(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
66	base change), then the comparison maps
67	\[
68	  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
69	  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
70	\]
71	are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
72	plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
73	allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
74	
75	The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
76	even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
77	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
78	formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
79	
80	\begin{enumerate}
81	  \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
82	    hypothesis. This is the formulation of
83	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
84	    in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
85	    proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
86	    rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
87	    over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
88	    hypothesis.
89	  \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
90	    rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
91	    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
92	    would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
93	    the \'etale site.
94	\end{enumerate}
95	
96	Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
97	being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
98	side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
99	
100	Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
101	rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
102	\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
103	
104	% SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4 (FGA Explained Ch.~9 \S 9.4);
105	% arXiv:math/0504020, p.~26. Read from
106	% references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex.
107	
108	\section{Line bundles and the Quot / Hilbert scheme}
109	\label{sec:fga_pic_line_bundle_quot}
110	
111	The bridge from line bundles on \(C \times_k T\) to the Quot scheme is the
112	Abel map: a relative effective divisor \(D \subset C \times_k T\) over \(T\)
113	(a \(T\)-flat closed subscheme whose ideal is invertible) determines a closed
114	subscheme of \(C \times_k T\) flat over \(T\), hence a \(T\)-point of the Hilbert
115	functor \(\Hilb_{C/k}(T)\), which is the special case \(\Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\)
116	of the Quot functor of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}; and it determines an
117	invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\) on the relative curve,
118	representing a class in \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T)\).

218	\section{The FGA representability theorem}
219	\label{sec:fga_pic_representability}
220	
221	We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck's existence theorem
222	for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian:
223	\(S = \Spec k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral
224	curve. The general theorem (Kleiman \S 4, Thm.~4.8) covers any
225	\(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric
226	fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise.

228	\begin{theorem}[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]\leanok
229	  \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}

232	        thm:quot_representable, def:rel_pic_sharp, def:has_rational_point,
233	        cor:flattening_stratification_curve, def:pic_sharp_representable,
234	        def:inst_pic_sharp_representable, lem:cech_flat_base_change}
235	  % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~th:main,
236	  % and Cor.~cor:algsch (specialisation to \(S = \Spec k\), \(X\) complete);
237	  % arXiv:math/0504020, pp.~26, 35 (read from
238	  % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex, L2155-L2166 + L2686-L2690).
239	  % Source identifiers: \begin{thm}\label{th:main}\end{thm}
240	  % and \begin{sbscor}\label{cor:algsch}\end{sbscor}.
241	  \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~4.8
242	  + Cor.~4.18.3.}
243	  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
244	  over \(k\) \emph{with a \(k\)-rational point}
245	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}). Then the relative Picard functor
246	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp} --- which under the
247	  rational-point hypothesis coincides with its \'etale sheafification
248	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), by Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 --- is representable by a
249	  \(k\)-scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over
250	  \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
251	  \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
252	  subschemes. The scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) is called the \emph{Picard scheme}
253	  of \(C/k\).
254	\end{theorem}
255	
256	\begin{proof}
257	  
258	  We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
259	  \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
260	  comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of
261	  \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme} and the relative Picard functor of
262	  \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
263	  correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.
264	
265	  \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
266	  By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
267	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}
268	  \mathcal O_{C \times_k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology
269	  and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of
270	  \(C\times_k T/T\)), the comparison map
271	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) \to \Pic_{(C/k)\et}(T)\) is bijective for all
272	  \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the \'etale sheaf
273	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which is what Kleiman's theorem produces; the same
274	  scheme then represents \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
275	
276	  \emph{Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.}
277	  For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq
278	  \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) be the \'etale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are
279	  represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) with
280	  \(\chi(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the
281	  Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation
282	  \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi\) form a
283	  disjoint open cover of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (openness via Kleiman's
284	  flat-base-change argument, \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change} / Stacks Tag 02KH;
285	  cf.\ EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to
286	  represent each \(P^\phi\) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective
287	  \(k\)-schemes.
288	
289	  \emph{Step 2: bound twists by \(m\)-regularity.}
290	  Given \(\phi\), fix \(m\) large enough that the \(T\)-points of \(P^\phi\) are
291	  representable by \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) satisfying
292	  \(R^i \pi_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0\) for all \(i \ge 1\), \(n \ge m\). Twisting
293	  by \(\mathcal{O}_C(m)\) defines an automorphism of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
294	  that carries \(P^\phi\) to \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) for \(\phi_0(n) := \phi(m + n)\).
295	  Hence it suffices to represent each \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) by a quasi-projective
296	  \(k\)-scheme.
297	
298	  \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}
299	  Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
300	  of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
301	  is representable by an open subscheme of \(\Hilb_{C/k}\) (and hence by an
302	  open subscheme of the Quot scheme of \cref{thm:quot_representable}), and
303	  is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along
304	  \(P^{\phi_0}_0 \hookrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) yields an open
305	  subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi_0}_0 \times_{\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
306	  of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection
307	  \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi_0}_0\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves:
308	  given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda\) of \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) represented by an \'etale
309	  cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times_k
310	  T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle
311	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to
312	  \(\mathcal{Q} := \pi_{T'*}\mathcal{L}'\) is smooth over \(T'\); an \'etale
313	  cover \(T_1 \to T'\) admits a \(T'\)-map \(T_1 \to \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q})\)
314	  (EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii)) whose composition with the universal divisor map
315	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to Z\) produces the required \(T_1\)-point of \(Z\).
316	  Moreover, the first projection \(Z \times_{P^{\phi_0}_0} Z \to Z\) is
317	  smooth and proper.
318	
319	  \emph{Step 4: descend by the smooth-proper quotient lemma.}
320	  Apply Kleiman~\S 4, Lem.~4.9: given a surjection \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
321	  of \'etale sheaves with \(Z\) quasi-projective, \(R := Z \times_P Z\)
322	  representable, and the first projection \(R \to Z\) smooth and proper,
323	  \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective scheme. In our case
324	  \(P = P^{\phi_0}_0\), \(Z\) and \(R\) as above, so \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) is
325	  quasi-projective. Reassembling over \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\) and
326	  over \(m\), the disjoint union of representable \(P^\phi\) pieces represents
327	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\). The total scheme is separated (as a disjoint
328	  union of separated quasi-projectives) and locally of finite type. This
329	  is Kleiman~\S 4, Cor.~4.18.3 in the \(S = \Spec k\),
330	  \(X = C\) complete case.
331	\end{proof}

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:relspec_setup}

The Route~A construction of \(J = \Pic^0_{C/k}\) as a \(g\)-dimensional abelian variety is
organised around the relative Picard functor
\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) = \Pic(C \times_k T) / \pi_T^* \Pic(T)\)
on the category of \(k\)-schemes. Representing \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) requires the line-bundle
pullback construction on a relative curve \(C \times_k T \to T\), which in turn rests on a
\emph{relative scheme} construction on a quasi-coherent sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-algebras
\(\mathcal{A}\), the \emph{relative spectrum}
\(\pi : \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A}) \to X\). This chapter packages the construction
of \(\underline{\Spec}_X(-)\) and its three core properties --- universal property, affine
base, base change --- as the foundational A.1.a building block. The relative Picard
functor itself (A.1.c), the line-bundle pullback functor on a product (A.1.b), and the
identity-component / dimension theory of \(J\) (A.3) live in separate sibling chapters
devoted to those constructions.
